C0.quote: first axiomatic characterization of a class of certification methods
C0.note: Aggregation of binary approval evaluations into a collective selection.

C1.quote: To formally assess the fundamental differences and similarities
C1.note: Both main results (Theorems 1, 2) are axiomatic characterizations.

C2.1.value: evaluation profile; evaluations; binary opinions; opinion profile
C2.1.quote: an evaluation profile on (N, X) collects the evaluations of the electorate

C2.2.quote: Each agent i ∈ N can either approve of an option
C2.2.note: Binary 0/1 evaluation for each option, equivalent to an approval set.

C2.3.quote: agents who are indifferent to all the options
C2.3.note: Attitude language (opinions, indifference) is used, but it is not defined separately from the evaluations.

C2.4.quote: members of a group express binary (i.e., yes-no, approval-disapproval) opinions
C2.4.note: Evaluations and opinions are treated as one object, and nothing is said about reporting. ONE would fit if 'evaluations' were read purely as ballots.

C4.1.note: No utility, welfare or satisfaction notions are used for voters.

C4.2.note: The term appears only in reference titles.

C5.1.quote: The next property is in the same spirit as the Pareto principle.
C5.1.note: Pareto consistency is a Pareto-type dominance axiom used in Lemma 3; borderline as an efficiency criterion.

C5.2.note: Dominance is defined on evaluation profiles.
